title: Functorial standard resolutions and comparison with arbitrary polynomial resolutions
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Let $F_A(E)=A[E]$ be the free polynomial algebra on a set $E$, let $U$ forget an algebra to its underlying set, and let $P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(B/A)$ be the augmented simplicial algebra with $P^{\mathrm{std}}_n=(F_AU)^{n+1}B$; its faces are induced by evaluation $F_AU\to\mathrm{id}$ and its degeneracies by the unit $\mathrm{id}\to UF_A$. For a simplicial module $M$, write $s(M)^{-n}=M_n$ with differential $\sum_i(-1)^id_i$ and zero positive terms. Define $L_{B/A}=s(\Omega^1_{P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet}B)$ in $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with differentials as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. The standard augmentation is a resolution. Here a polynomial resolution $P_\bullet\to B$ means that every $P_n$ is a polynomial $A$-algebra surjecting onto $B$ and $s(P_\bullet)\to B[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For every such resolution there is a canonical comparison isomorphism $s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B)\simeq L_{B/A}$, natural for morphisms of augmented polynomial resolutions. A commutative square of ring maps $A\to B$, $A'\to B'$, $A\to A'$, $B\to B'$ induces a canonical semilinear map $P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(B/A)\to P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(B'/A')$ commuting with the augmentations, hence a map of differential complexes. These standard maps preserve identities and compose strictly; the induced maps in derived categories agree with the maps obtained using polynomial resolutions and their canonical comparisons.

source.place: Tags 08PM (definition-standard-resolution), 08PN (definition-cotangent-complex-ring-map), 08QI (remark-resolution), 08QL (section-functoriality), especially the explicit maps A[B] to A′[B′].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-adjunction-standard-simplicial-homotopy] to the adjunction $F_A:\mathrm{Set}\rightleftarrows A\text{-}\mathrm{Alg}:U$; its adjunction bijection sends an algebra map $A[E]\to C$ to its values on the variables. This gives exactly the faces, degeneracies and augmentation in the statement, and gives a simplicial-set homotopy inverse to the underlying standard augmentation. Each term is polynomial. Each evaluation $A[UC]\to C$ is surjective because $[c]\mapsto c$; iterating these evaluations shows that every standard augmentation is surjective. The unit is a map of sets; no additivity of this section is asserted.

A simplicial homotopy equivalence $f:X\to Y$ is a weak homotopy equivalence in the precise sense of [lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence]: precomposition on $\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(-,W)$ for every Kan $W$ has inverse induced by a chosen homotopy inverse of $f$. Indeed composing a homotopy $H:X\times\Delta[1]\to X$ with $X\to W$ gives an edge between the corresponding maps, so the two composites induce the identity on these components. Apply this to the standard augmentation from Step 1. Regard its rings only as simplicial $\mathbf Z$-modules. By [lem-cbc-simplicial-module-model], weak equivalences are created on underlying simplicial sets and are exactly the maps whose normalized complexes are quasi-isomorphisms. By the natural homotopy equivalence from normalized to alternating complexes in [lem-cbc-normalized-alternating-homotopy-equivalence], the alternating augmentation is therefore a quasi-isomorphism too. The alternating complex of a constant module $B$ maps quasi-isomorphically onto $B[0]$: in positive homological degrees its differentials alternate between zero and the identity. Hence the standard augmentation is a resolution in the required sense.

source.place: Tag 08P2; comparison of normalized and alternating complexes; cotangent lemma-identify-L-pi-shriek

proof.text: For any polynomial resolution $Q\to B$, its underlying simplicial abelian-group map is termwise surjective and its alternating complex map to the constant simplicial module $B$ is a quasi-isomorphism (use the constant-complex calculation in Step 2). The natural equivalence [lem-cbc-normalized-alternating-homotopy-equivalence] makes its normalized map a quasi-isomorphism. It is also surjective in each normalized degree: lift a normalized element to $x\in Q_n$ and, for $k=n,n-1,\ldots,1$, replace $x$ by $x-s_{k-1}d_kx$. The simplicial identities show that this kills $d_kx$ while preserving the already zero faces $d_jx$ for $j>k$; its image in $B_n$ stays the chosen normalized element. Thus [lem-cbc-simplicial-module-model] makes this a trivial fibration, and the underlying simplicial-set map a trivial fibration as well, since both fibrations and weak equivalences are created there. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], these are precisely the maps with the boundary lifting property, including degree zero, i.e. trivial Kan fibrations as defined in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration].

Choose universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ as in [def-weil-size-convention], with the rings and all the resolutions in question $\mathcal U$-small. Let $\mathcal D_{B/A}$ have as objects all $\mathcal U$-small polynomial $A$-algebras $T$ equipped with an $A$-algebra map $T\to B$ (not required to be surjective), and as arrows algebra maps over $B$. All their structure data and maps form sets in $\mathcal V$, so this is a small category there; complexes and modules below are taken in $\mathcal V$. A resolution is a simplicial object of this category. For $T=A[E]\to B$, maps $T\to Q_n$ over $B$ are precisely choices, for every $e\in E$, of an element of $Q_n$ mapping to the prescribed image of $e$ in $B$. This bijection commutes with all simplicial operators, by evaluation on generators.

source.place: Category of polynomial presentations in section-comparison; Tag 08PS and its size-bound footnote; a containing universe is used here

proof.text: The simplicial set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_{B/A}}(T,Q_\bullet)$ maps to a singleton by a trivial Kan fibration. To check the boundary lifting condition of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], a boundary of algebra maps is, on each generator $e$, a boundary in $Q$ above the constant simplex $\epsilon_T(e)\in B$. Step 3 supplies a filler for each generator; choose these fillers and extend them uniquely to an algebra map out of $A[E]$. This gives the required filler of algebra maps, and degree-zero surjectivity is proved by the same choice of generator lifts. This works for an empty set or an infinite set of generators, without finite-generation assumptions. Now [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] supplies a homotopy equivalence with the singleton. This argument applies both to $Q$ and to the standard resolution.

source.place: Tag 08PS (lemma-identify-pi-shriek), the generator-fibre argument; simplicial Tag 08NS

proof.text: Define the covariant functor $\mathcal F_{B/A}(T)=\Omega^1_{T/A}\otimes_T B$ on $\mathcal D_{B/A}$. An arrow $v:T\to T'$ induces $dt\otimes b\mapsto d(vt)\otimes b$; existence and equality under composition follow from the universal derivation in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Set $K(Q)=s(\mathcal F_{B/A}(Q_\bullet))$ and $H_{B/A}=\mathbf H(\mathcal D_{B/A},\mathcal F_{B/A})$. Steps 4 and 5 verify precisely the smallness and representable-contractibility assumptions of [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-colimit-computation]. Its isomorphisms are $a_Q:K(Q)\simeq H_{B/A}$ and $a_{\mathrm{std}}:L_{B/A}\simeq H_{B/A}$. Define $c_Q=a_{\mathrm{std}}^{-1}a_Q$. Its naturality says $a_R K(h)=a_Q$ for any augmented resolution morphism $h:Q\to R$, so $c_R K(h)=c_Q$. This proves the canonical comparison and its naturality in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No maps in both directions between arbitrary algebra resolutions have been assumed.

For a ring square $(\alpha:A\to A',\beta:B\to B')$, define $t_{-1}=\beta$ and recursively $t_{n+1}:A[UP_n]\to A'[UP'_n]$ by $a\mapsto\alpha(a)$ and $[p]\mapsto[t_n(p)]$; similarly $t_0:A[UB]\to A'[UB']$. Evaluation commutes with these maps because both composites send $[p]$ to $t_n(p)$. Insertion of the unit commutes as well because both composites send a variable to the variable labelled by its image. Applying this at the relevant iteration gives commutation with every face, degeneracy and augmentation. For an identity square the recursion fixes coefficients and variables; for two squares the composite recursion sends $[p]$ to $[t'_nt_n(p)]$. Uniqueness of a map from a polynomial algebra with specified generator values therefore gives strict identity and composition in every degree. Finally the rule $dp\otimes b\mapsto d(t_np)\otimes\beta(b)$ is balanced and kills the relative-derivation relations, by [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; it gives the required semilinear map of differential complexes and preserves those strict identities.

source.place: Section Functoriality, Tag 08QL; explicit map P_0=A[B] to A′[B′] and its iteration

proof.text: The square also defines a functor $u:\mathcal D_{B/A}\to\mathcal D_{B'/A'}$ by $T\mapsto T\otimes_A A'$ with augmentation $t\otimes a'\mapsto\beta(\epsilon_T(t))a'$. It remains polynomial: $A[E]\otimes_A A'\simeq A'[E]$, as follows from the mutually inverse maps fixing coefficients and variables. The maps $dt\otimes b\mapsto d(t\otimes1)\otimes\beta(b)$ define $\theta:\mathcal F_{B/A}\to\operatorname{Res}_\beta(\mathcal F_{B'/A'}\circ u)$ by [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. A supplied semilinear augmented simplicial map $h:Q\to Q'$ gives $k:uQ\to Q'$ by $q\otimes a'\mapsto h(q)a'$, and the standard map of Step 7 gives such a $k$ for the standard resolutions. Neither $uQ$ nor its augmentation is claimed to be a resolution: only the endpoints $Q,Q'$ need be resolutions.

source.place: Functoriality: category of polynomial presentations and u(P)=P⊗_A A′, following Tag 08QL

proof.text: Apply the reindexing naturality clause of [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-colimit-computation] to the data of Step 8. Write $H(\alpha,\beta)=\mathbf H(u,\theta)$. It gives $a_{Q'}K(h)=H(\alpha,\beta)a_Q$; for standard resolutions it gives $a'_{\mathrm{std}}K(t)=H(\alpha,\beta)a_{\mathrm{std}}$. Restriction of scalars is understood on every target. Substituting $c_Q=a_{\mathrm{std}}^{-1}a_Q$ and $c_{Q'}=(a'_{\mathrm{std}})^{-1}a_{Q'}$ yields $c_{Q'}K(h)=K(t)c_Q$. Thus whenever a map between chosen resolutions is supplied it gives exactly the standard derived map through the canonical comparisons. For arbitrary choices of resolutions define the transported map by $c_{Q'}^{-1}K(t)c_Q$; the same equation proves agreement with every supplied $h$. Its identity law is $c_Q^{-1}c_Q=1$, and its composition law follows by cancelling the middle $c_{Q'}c_{Q'}^{-1}$ and using the strict composition of Step 7. Changing resolutions is likewise transitive by cancelling the common factor. This proves the final compatibility clause without asserting the existence of algebra homotopy inverses.
